ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If the herbivores were removed from this food chain, which group would see the greatest benefit?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a bottom-up food chain. The bottom box is labeled “Plants,” with an arrow above it pointing to “Herbivores”; further upward, an arrow points to “Primary Carnivores”; the top arrow points to “Secondary Carnivores.” Next to the arrows is labeled “10%,” indicating that energy is transferred upward along the food chain. Reasoning: Herbivores feed on plants. If herbivores are removed, the feeding pressure on plants will decrease, so the number or growth condition of plants is most likely to improve; while primary and secondary carnivores will lose or have reduced food sources and will not benefit the most. Therefore, the group that benefits the most is plants.
